utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is the decision of the Trial Chamber on the issue of the admissibility of statements under Rule 92 bis. We have considered the Prosecution motion for the admissibility of 23 statements under the Rule. In principle, we will admit the statements under the Rule, but subject to two conditions. The first is this: Because of the cumulative nature of the evidence and the fact that it will increase the already very extensive number of witnesses proposed to be called by the Prosecution in this case, and bearing in mind the need for an expeditious trial, the Prosecution will be limited to four witnesses per municipality, including the viva voce witnesses already called. The Prosecution is to select which of the Rule 92 bis statements it wishes to have admitted for those municipalities where at the moment it is proposed more than four witnesses. The second condition is this: Because, in the view of the Trial Chamber, the evidence proposed to be given is subject of an important issue in this case, those witnesses whose statements are admitted will be required to attend for cross-examination, the Prosecution being allowed in each case to ask some introductory questions. Written reasons for this decision will follow in due course. We shall also consider any necessary adjustment to the timetable for finishing the Prosecution case and any application to extend the number of witnesses, on good cause being shown. Mr. Ryneveld, we've just been handed a summary of a witness. It appears that there's going to be another change in the order; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of, beyond the list that we provided the other day. The one thing that may have happened, Your Honour, is that my understanding is that once the present witness, Mr. Loku, is finished, we will call Mr. Bucaliu, followed -- depending on how long that takes, there is a -- we anticipate calling Dr. Ball tomorrow. If there is time left at the end of the day, we might have the opportunity of moving up another witness. But that was more a consideration to accommodate the accused's concern about getting the B/C/S translation of the document, and we thought that giving him an extra evening of preparation time might well be of assistance. However, it's hard to predict whether we'll even get that far today. But in the event we do, that is a possibility. I trust that meets with the Trial Chamber's approval.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you. I propose, then, to continue with Mr. Loku at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let's have the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Ryneveld: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Loku, yesterday before we broke for the day with your evidence, I had asked you, if I recall correctly, whether upon your return from Macedonia you returned to your village of Kotlina, and I believe you indicated you had, and you told us that you found your village to be destroyed. Am I -- is that a fair summary of what you told us yesterday?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, I believe at that point I asked you whether or not you had brought some photographs with you to The Hague, and I'm going to show you now some enlargements of those photographs, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: And we have, first of all -- yes. Thank you. Just so the Court knows, I intend to show him the first of three photographs. That's it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 56.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Clerk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you're looking at a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Might that be placed on the ELMO, Mr. Usher. Is it coming up yet? I don't know if the ELMO is operating, Your Honour. We're not getting a picture. There we are.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, here it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sir, first of all, is that a photograph that you brought with you?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a photograph I brought.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do we see in this photograph? What is that a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we had received this photograph earlier, all of us, in the documents that we see -- that we received several months ago. We had received these photographs earlier. Therefore, I don't see what the problem is here now. Why are we asking this gentleman whether he brought these photographs in? Because we've had these photographs for several months now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let him describe what the photographs are.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, what is this a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photograph of the burned school where I used to work. After we returned from Macedonia, we cleaned it up. This is the photograph of the burned and destroyed school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And that's in Kotlina; correct?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's in Kotlina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to show you now another photograph, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Mr. Usher. Perhaps we could give both sets now so it will save time. Could you distribute those two photographs. And could the first of those be placed on the ELMO and shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, we can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is another photograph that you brought with you, sir, and we've had enlarged; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us what is shown in this particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, what is the objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the objection is, Your Honours, that these photographs already exist. I don't see what kind of an explanation this is, that the witness brought them in now. These are photographs that we received several months ago. Isn't that undeniable?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You may have received them, but the Court has not seen them, and we don't know what they are. The witness must be allowed to explain what the photographs are. Now, we'll get on more quickly without interruption.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no, I agree, Your Honour. That's quite correct. But I don't understand what this means when they say that the witness brought these photographs in today. I'm asking this because there are some things I would like to touch upon later. I don't find this clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can ask him in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what is this a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph shows villagers returning after their expulsion to Macedonia. It shows them assembled, and in front of them there are the coffins which were later taken for burial. They are the burial of the people who were massacred and who were exhumed by the Tribunal and were prepared for burial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the building in the foreground, more or less immediately behind the row of people, what is that? What building was that?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Behind the people, there is the house of Baki Kuqi, a two-storey house. You can see two entrances from the road. It's the shop, and the other part is the residence, the dwelling part of the building. This house is separated from the school only by the road. It's on the other side of the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this building destroyed during the course of the events that you described to us in your evidence yesterday?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this -- I'm sorry. The final of the three photographs, sir, I take it that --

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Do we have that yet? Has it been distributed? Will you please distribute the final photograph, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This photograph will be numbered Exhibit 57. The present photograph, Exhibit 58.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you look at this photograph, please, Exhibit 58, Witness. Is this another slightly different angle, a shot of the same building in the background on the right?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a photograph of the same building, but you can here see the yard and the coffins which are here, have been brought from Kacanik, and here are the people on the street, waiting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. Now, just one question about those photographs. Did you personally take them or were they given to you to bring with you?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took them myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you take them?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took these photographs when I came back from where I was. There were a lot of photographs of this kind when we went to the funeral.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And the month and the year in which you took these photographs, please?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: These photographs must be from September, when the funeral took place. I don't remember the date, but it was September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was 1999, was it, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the same year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, one final issue, sir. I want to back you up to -- you've told us about witnessing an explosion after the men were put into the two holes you talked about yesterday. Upon your return, sir, did you find out who was missing in your village?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was while we were in Macedonia that we really found out who was missing, by asking relatives, and then we counted 22 people who were missing. And then, later, they were brought out of the pits for examination, although some people hoped that some of their relatives would in fact have survived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were the bodies that were taken out of the pits identified, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe they all were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say that you saw these young men being thrown into the pits; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your vantage point, could you tell their identities as they were being thrown in? Could you see who they were?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what you saw at the time they were being thrown into the holes, could you see who those young men were who were being thrown in the holes? Did you know them? Did you know them by name?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew the names of each one of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you brought with you photographs of the names of the people who you say were thrown in the holes?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I brought a photograph of each one of them, except for one of whom I couldn't find a photograph because all of the photographs were burned in their house. But I have brought photographs of all the others, and I can identify them. I grew up with them and I knew them all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the one person for whom you could not find a photograph, is that an individual that you mentioned in your evidence yesterday?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And his name?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name is Idriz Kuqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Schedule L, the first name, Your Honours. There's no photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, these -- you brought us, I believe, some 24 photographs, individual small photographs, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have seen that we have prepared five pages of a collage of those photographs? You've seen that?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I propose now to produce a further exhibit, with a legend, and perhaps we can make these five pages of photographs one exhibit number. And there's also a legend that will go with it. I don't want the legend shown to the witness, but I want the Court to have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Loku, you'll see that there are some five pages of photographs of individuals. Do you recognise those photographs as being copies of the ones that you brought with you? Just quickly look at the pages. Are those copies of the photographs you brought?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And could you tell us, please, looking at the photograph -- each of these photographs now has a number above the photograph. Can you tell us, please, the name of the individual, starting with photograph 1. Who is that?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1 is Adnan Loku.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's on the schedule. Now, Adnan, I believe in the schedule it's spelled A-t-a-n. Is that a correct spelling of the first name, sir, or is it Adnan, A-d-a-n [sic]?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Adnan, A-d-n-a-n, with "d." Adnan.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I believe that's the sixth name down on the Schedule L, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Photograph number 2, who is that?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 2 and number 8 are brothers. One 16 and one 17. One of them is called Ibush and the other is Naser. I could get the names mixed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Those names are on Schedule L, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Loku is their surname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Photograph number 3, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 3 is Mina Kuqi, a school pupil.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have the legend. We have the photographs. Unless there's any dispute about it, I don't think we need go through them all. We shall, of course, look at them, and we will be able to see ourselves what the photographs show.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes. That may well be a better course of proceeding, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I just have a couple questions of clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ryneveld, I just wanted to find out a question. On the legend, several names similar to the witness's. Are these relatives?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I asked that question, Your Honour, and perhaps we should have the witness --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Many of these people, sir, that you have talked about have the same last name as you. Are any of them relatives or is "Loku" a common name in Kotlina?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could tell you about each one of them. Number 2 and number 8 are the brothers Ibush and Naser Loku. They were the sons of Rexhep whom I talked about yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they were relatives of yours?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Really close cousins, but they were from the same village. There were two other brothers, Agim and Ismajl Loku. There were a lot of them who were each other's cousins and who happened to be together. There are cousins Danush Kuqi, who is a secondary school pupil. That's number 10. Xhemjal Kuqi, number 12. He was his cousin. Sherif Kuqi, 11, was a cousin, and Ismajl. Number 21 was his cousin, a closer cousin. They were first cousins of each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I go on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I just wanted to know how many of them were relatives of yours. It appears that some of them were. Thank you, Mr. Ryneveld.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, for example, number -- photograph 23 --

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Kuqi family were cousins among themselves, not my cousins.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Except for -- as I understand it, sir, you told us yesterday that Zymer Loku, number 23, he was not found in the holes was he? You told us, I believe, that you personally found him in a -- in a house. He was wounded and died later.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Photograph 22 was the 72-year-old man Zymer Loku. He was wounded, fatally wounded, and his right leg was cut off, and we found him in the house yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And similarly, 23 is your brother Milaim Loku?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the photograph of my brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he also was not in the holes?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was in the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Given Your Honour's comments about the legend, I might just have one further question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, there are -- these are the 24 photographs you brought with you, which include two people who were not in the holes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. How about number 1? Idriz Kuqi was also shot in a separate place.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: That's the one for whom he did not have a photograph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe those are -- given Your Honour's comments, you have the legend. If the legend can also go in, then, as part of the exhibit, I believe that obviates the need for any further exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 60 and the legend 60A.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The microphone wasn't switched on. Thank you. Before I start asking my questions, I should like to draw your attention to the following: This is an example of a manipulation with semi-truths on behalf of the Prosecution which must not be allowed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is not the time for comment, Mr. Milosevic. That Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. point has been made quite clear. It's the time to ask questions. Now, if you've got matters to put to the witness, put it to him so he can deal with it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Don't worry. I can do that through my questions as well. Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You worked as a professor in the school and technical centre in Kacanik; is that right? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked there for two years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you work in the actual school building or in a private house?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where I was working, I was in the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also worked in Kotlina as a teacher; is that right? Did you work there in the school building or in a private house there?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in both cases, you used the state school building and not private houses; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the two places where I worked, I worked in the schools.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you know about the fact that in Kotlina there was the main headquarters for transferring weapons from Macedonia, that it was located in Kotlina?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a lie of yours. It is not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is it from Kotlina to the Macedonian border?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 12 to 15 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is located at about five kilometres from Kacanik, on the right-hand side of the main road running from Pristina to Skopje; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's on the right as you go from Prishtina to Skopje. I don't know how far. Maybe, as the crow flies, five kilometres, no more. I don't think it's five. On the road that I travel, it's three or four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So much the better. The village of Kotlina is adjoining to the village of Kotlanica [phoen], which is where the crossing to Macedonia is on the Urosevac-Tetovo road on the slopes of Mount Sharre; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is a road to Gllobocica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Kotlina, via the village of Ivaja, is linked to Jezerce, is that right, across Ivaja?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Jezerci is far away, in Ferizaj mountains. It's another way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is it from Kotlina, I mean?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you a figure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Roughly.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ferizaj is some 30 kilometres away from Kacanik. We are closer to the border. Maybe it's some 40 or 50 kilometres from Elez Han.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm asking you about Jezerce. What's 50 kilometres away from you? Kotlina?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since you asked me -- I thought you asked me about the distance between Kotlina and Jezerci, if I'm right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. How far is Kotlina from Jezerce?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think 40 kilometres. I've never been there. I can't give you an exact figure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know -- are you familiar with the position and role of Jezerce in Kotlina during the war and before the war?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding Jezerci, I might say that in summer, or earlier, we heard the shelling of it, but I don't know exactly what went on there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Jezerce was one of the main strongholds of the KLA for the entire region of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard that KLA was stationed there, but I can't tell more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go back now to your municipality. As you worked in the municipality and in the school, do you happen to know that in the municipality, 85 people were employed, 62 of them were Albanians? Are you aware of that figure?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never worked in the municipality myself, so this is what you are saying. I have always worked in the education sector. I lived in the municipality in the last years of my life. Even though our municipality was 99.99 composed of Albanian population, none of us worked there, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the municipality there were 85 employees, of which 62 were Albanians, and as far as the figures that you have put forward, that figure is incorrect. There were 2 per cent Serbs, which would make it about 300 -- not about, but 335 Serbs and about a thousand Romany. Are you aware of that, of those figures and that information?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of any figures, and I don't know that these people used to work in the municipality. When I had to go to the commune to take some documents, I always encountered only Serbs there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that in the Sharre factory at Djeneral Jankovic, right next to your village, of the 1.700 workers, more than 1.500 were Albanians?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were Albanians in the past, but lately it was full of Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How could it have been full of Serbs when you said a moment ago that there were no Serbs in that municipality of yours?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the municipality, but they came from Shterpce commune, and the Albanians who worked there were fired from their jobs and sent home. There were three villagers of mine who were close neighbours, and they were fired from their jobs and stayed at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they fired from?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I really don't know in Kacanik what the situation was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just answer the question, if you would. You said they were fired from their jobs and sent home, including three neighbours of yours, and the question is: Which jobs were they fired from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They used to work in this factory, doing various jobs. That was a cement-producing factory, and they did various jobs there. One was a mechanic, one was in another workshop there, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's clear this matter up. I say that of the 1.700 workers, there were more than 1.500 Albanians working in the factory right up until the war. Is that true or not? Yes or no. One thousand, five hundred were Albanians.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never worked in that factory, and I can't give you exact figures, but when we went to the marketplace on Wednesday, we always used to see Serbs driving to and from that plant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And are you aware of the fact that in Kacanik, there were more than 300 members of the Socialist Party of Serbia; of that number, 220 were Albanians; and the secretary of the board was somebody called Hanka Luka, an Albanian lady? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of that. I was never myself a member of that party, so I don't know anything about its membership.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in Kacanik, an Albanian party was set up, and it was called the Albanian Democratic Initiative, and the president of that party was Faik Jashari? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This name doesn't ring a bell. I don't remember anything about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me remind you. Faik Jashari was also a member of the state delegation in Rambouillet, at the negotiations that were held in Rambouillet. Do you remember that? Does that ring a bell? Does that help you identify the person I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think you are fabricating such names. I don't know of any names like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just deal with the questions, please. We'll get on more quickly. Yes, Mr. Milosevic, we've dealt with this question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in Kacanik a local police force was set up made up exclusively of the representatives of the Albanian ethnic group and a small number of Romany? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that, from the village of Kotlina, the coordinators for the local police force were Bashkim Loku. He has the same surname as you do. His father's name was Sulejman. So Bashkim Sulejman Loku, and Shaban Zenujlla Kuqi. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know these persons personally. I never knew they were policemen because I've never seen them wearing uniforms. They are both alive to this day; one living in Kotlina, the other in Ferizaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that members of that local police force were exposed to constant threats and attacks by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: What happened in the Serb police I know nothing about, but I don't know they were in any way endangered by someone else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was the Albanian police. According to my information, 12 members of the local police force were killed or kidnapped by the KLA, and my question is do you know any one of these people: Nisem Tusha, Alia was his father's name. So it is Nisem Alia Tusha. Osman Kuka. The father's name Xheladia [phoen]. Bektish Melushe Dardiste [phoen]. Selim Agusha Topolani. Shajip Emina Reka. Riza Faik Kiki. Bedri Shefki Berisha, Qamil Emin Reka [phoen], Gazim Azem Sinanovic [phoen], Dalip Emin Reka, Shaban Zenujlla Kuqi, and Baskim Sulejman Loku. Have you heard of any of these people? Do you know any of these names? They were all local policeman. As you can see, they were all Albanians and some Romany, one or two Romany. Do you know anything whatsoever about these people?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I know the two names you mentioned earlier. They are my co-villagers. I know them in person. They are alive to this day. As far as the other names are concerned, I can't tell you anything. I don't know if they were police in uniforms, regular police, that is. They were policemen. They must be in Serbia somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the fact that the KLA, according to the local security, and they were a local police force, so not members of the Ministry for the Interior, do you know because -- that because of their relationship towards the local security people and generally the members of the Albanian community who were loyal to the state, that the KLA, first of all in the village of Ivaja and then in Kotlina, formed prisons for them, set up prisons for these people? So I'm talking about Ivaja and Kotlina, those two villages, the ones that you mention in your testimony.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never heard of that, and I don't -- and I don't think that that was true. What you are saying, these people who are police, they must have been staying with the police. So I know nothing about them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in the village of Ivaja, in a prison of that kind, they found and released a group of 15 Albanians who were prisoners there? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I've never heard anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Talks were held with them and there is a videotape about that, but you heard nothing of that? Fifteen Albanians?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He says he knows nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know about the fact that before the NATO bombing in Kacanik, there were many Albanians who were loyal to Serbia, a large number of them, and that a group of -- in the summer of 1977 [as interpreted] sent letters of support, and also in the spring of 1998 also sent a letter of support to the authorities, energetically calling for the suppression of Albanian terrorism? Do you know about that? It was written up in all the papers which were sold in Kacanik, and it was from the municipality of Kacanik that the event came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The date -- one date has been translated for these letters of the summer of 1977.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: 1997; very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next expression of support was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness deal with the question so far. What is said is that in the summer of 1997 and the spring of 1998, letters of support were written from Kacanik, calling for suppression of Albanian terrorism. Can you assist us about that or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know nothing of what he is saying. Nobody told me that there was any such letters written. Those who have -- who may have written those letters might know something. I know nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Forty-eight Albanians and Romany sent that letter, and that took place on the 23rd of March, 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He says he knows nothing about the letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know about a decision of the Executive Council of Kosovo and Metohija dating to February 1999, a February 1999 decision stipulating that the Municipal Assembly of Kacanik should give out free of charge land for individual housing construction to Albanians who were citizens of the SRY -- FRY? Sorry. Who were citizens of Yugoslavia, in fact.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never read any Serb papers, so I know nothing about that either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know that people built houses on that land, that Albanians, Yugoslav citizens, built houses on that land that they got free of charge?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that in my own village, everybody built his own home in his own land, and nobody assisted them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that, afterwards, the KLA destroyed these houses of theirs because they built it on state-owned land? Do you know anything about an event of that nature, anything similar?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing that -- I know nothing about it, and it seems absurd to me what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is probably so. Do you know that during July and August 1998, two large groups of terrorists were arrested, both coming from Urosevac and Kacanik? They were arrested by the police. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was all the time minding my own business. I went to school and went back home, and I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember - it's not a big town, after all - in December 1998, by the village of Dimce near the border with Macedonia, when a large quantity of weapons was seized? I'm linking this to the first question, that Kotlina was used as the main channel for obtaining weapons from Macedonia. So in December 1998, by the village of Dimce at the border with Macedonia, a large quantity of weapons was seized, and on that occasion the following persons were arrested: Berisha Valon --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Let the -- let the witness deal with the question. You were asked about December 1998, and it is alleged that there was a seizure of a large quantity of weapons at Dimce. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dimce is on the other bank of the river. It's far away from where I live. I've heard that there are Serb police stationed there and that in Han i Elezit they arrested some people, but I don't know the motive for that. And usually we didn't trust the Serb media because usually there was a lot of propaganda on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I said Dimce at the border with Macedonia. Usually what is seized is something that is illegally being taken across the border.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. What is the next question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question was: Does he know these persons who were arrested, that is to say, Berisha Valon, Berisha Ekrem, and Topolani Naser?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never knew these people. I know nothing about them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: None of them are from Kotlina?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none of them is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know all the inhabitants of Kotlina, don't you?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of what happened in February 1999 when, in the village of Djurdjev Do, the KLA attacked a police patrol? Three policemen were wounded then, and five members of the KLA were killed. Do you remember that event in February 1999?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember that on the 20th of February, 1999, around 9.00 in the evening, that is to say 9.00 p.m., Selim Topolani was kidnapped from his own house and taken out of it barefoot? He was president of the Albanian Democratic Initiative for Kacanik.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm unable to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we've been through this with other witnesses. This witness cannot help as to these various allegations you're making. You will have the opportunity in due course to -- you will have the opportunity in due course to present evidence. You've put your case very fully to him. Now, I suggest you move on and deal much more with his evidence. Time is not limitless.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's precisely what I'm dealing with, his statement, because all of these terrorist actions preceded the event that the witness is treating as a central event, and now we're getting go that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware on the 27th of February that in the village of Gajre a member of the local guard was abducted, and he also worked in the factory called Krecara, Riza Kiki? An ethnic Albanian as well.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know on the 28th of February, around 1300 hours, again in the village of Gajre, a large group of terrorists attacked the police, who were going out looking for Riza Kiki, and on that occasion the commander of the police, Bobuljub Staletevic [phoen], was killed and three policemen were seriously wounded; then a terrorist was also killed, Asaj Etema, from the village of Gabrice - he was in uniform and he had a hand-held launcher with two grenades that had not been fired - and the rest escaped? Do you remember that incident?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear that something happened at Gajre. During that time, the Serb patrols used to torture the people, and I heard that something happened, but I can't give you any names about the victims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So now we've reached the end of February, the first days of March, the kidnapping of Topolani, the kidnapping of the local policemen, the killing of a police patrol, and now we are getting to this beginning of March that you had been talking about. Is it correct what I'm going to state right now: that fighting was taking place in that area, that the KLA was emptying villages, using empty houses as fortified positions, which necessarily led to the fact that they were shooting at the police from there, and this therefore made the Serb Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. forces react to that? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what happened there, but as for my village, I can answer about my village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Help us with this, Mr. Loku: Was there any reason that you could see for the attack which took place at the beginning of March and on the 24th of March on your village? Was there any background to that which might explain it, as far as you're concerned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my view, there was no reason for my village to be attacked.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You haven't answered my question. The KLA emptied villages, used empty houses - and I'm including the village of Ivaja there, the one that you started with - they used empty houses as fortified positions, which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He said, Mr. Milosevic, in answer to that: "I don't know what happened there, but as for my village, I can answer about my village." That was his answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but may I remind you, then, that here he stated that the village of Ivaja was attacked, and he's from the village of Kotlina, which is near Ivaja, and he started his whole story with the attack on the village of Ivaja, and that's what I'm referring to now. As for what I've just read, I read it from the report of the Verification Mission of the OSCE. But now I shall go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this assertion correct: "Although it seemed that the villagers were on the side of the KLA, there were reports that local people were forced to show support for or join the KLA." Is that correct or not, what I've just read out to you? Just say yes or no, make a comment, whatever you prefer.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying either yes -- the truth is, around the mountains of Ivaja, the KLA was present. They had gone out voluntarily. Nobody forced them. They could no longer stand the tortures to which the Serbian forces submitted the population. Anybody who wished joined the KLA. That is what I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A short while ago I quoted to you how the KLA emptied houses and turned them into fortifications, from which they were shooting at the army and the police, and that's what this report says as well. That's why I'm saying that the explanation is a manipulated one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, this is all comment. You can put the report in front of us in due course, but for the moment confine yourself to asking questions of this witness. He said he doesn't know anything about what's written in the report. Now, can you move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's precisely what I've been talking about. What is the key point in the witness's statement is some kind of an attack on Ivaja and then Kotlina, caused by nothing, according to him. It was all actually the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is his evidence. Now, you put your evidence in front of us and we'll consider it, but there's no point arguing with the witness when he's given his evidence, given his account. Now, can you move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. I'm just asking about Kotlina. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the KLA detained, against their own free will, in the village of Kotlina, refugees? They were not allowed to leave, although the KLA and the UNHCR had an agreement on safe passage for refugees outside the areas of conflict. Are you aware of that, that villagers, refugees in Kotlina - I'm talking about the beginning of March - were not allowed to leave Kotlina? The KLA didn't allow them to do this, although the KLA had an agreement with the UNHCR on safe passage for these people to get out of the zone of conflict.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This has been made up. No villagers were kept hostage by anybody. I was in this village. They remained freely in their houses. They had no reason to go anywhere. When fighting began nearby, we tried to get away, but you killed us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, what is written here and what I've read out to you: The KLA did not allow people to leave the zone of conflict --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He has said it's not true. Now, we can't go further than that. It's his answer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. All right, Mr. May. I'm just drawing your attention to the fact that this is written in the OSCE report, the Kosovo Verification Mission report dated the 11th of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have been through that. In due course you can put that report in, but for the moment you're asking this witness questions and you've got his answer. There's no good going on about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The question was about the refugees from other villages, not about the villagers of Kotlina. Could you answer that? Were any refugees kept hostage by KLA in your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, there weren't any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After these clashes, when the verifiers finally got to your village, managed to visit Kotlina, that is, they found the inhabitants of Kotlina there and many displaced persons from nearby hamlets. They claim that then the bodies of three men were found, who were identified as members of the KLA. Is that correct? Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our village, there was never any clashes between anyone. On 10th of March, the OSCE Verification Mission members came. They took some old people and women of Dreshec neighbourhood, that was burned down, and took them to Kacanik. We asked them that they take us away too, to some safer place, but they told us that Kacanik was full of refugees from other hamlets and there was no place for any more refugees. So they told us, "Stay where you are, because we will take care of you." And this is what happened. Until the 23rd of March, they stayed in our village and we felt safe. That was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this incident, that is to say, when the Mission came, the OSCE mission, when they came to your village, do you know when the problem came up when the commander of the KLA did not allow the UNHCR access to displaced persons in your village, in the village of Kotlina? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember to have seen any KLA members there. I am saying that there wasn't any KLA members there. I said that OSCE observers came, and they removed -- displaced some people of that neighbourhood that was burned down. As for the rest, we stayed there. You had better ask the OSCE observers. They might give you a better version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since I wasn't there either, I'm asking you about what I read in the report submitted by the OSCE monitors. They had a problem. The KLA did not allow the UNHCR access to displaced persons in Kotlina. So you know nothing of this; right?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know only that the OSCE monitors came to Kotlina, took away some people - nobody prevented them - and that when we asked them to help all of us, to take all of us to Kacanik, as I said, they said that there is no more room there to shelter more people, because people were coming in from the surrounding villages every day. So they told us that it is rife with refugees, Kacanik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now I'm going to put a specific question to you, without beating about the bush. This also stems from the report of the OSCE. It says: "Although the problem had been resolved and the representative of the KLA apologised, there were also indications that the KLA was responsible for such a large number of refugees because they used these villages as the front line of the conflict itself." So do you know anything about this? Do you know why the KLA used the village as a front line of the conflict itself?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that has been true of the KLA, because the KLA members were staying in the mountains. And we were not refugees. We were residents of the village. We were staying in our own homes. We were not afraid of KLA, because we looked upon them as our defenders. We were afraid of the Serb forces, police and army forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: What do you know about the use of village houses as the front line in the conflict between the KLA, on the one hand, and the army and the police on the other hand? What do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This has never happened in my village. There were no KLA members and no confrontations between them and the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the basis of what the report of the Verification Mission says, it seems to have been the other way around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness said -- the witness has given his answer. Can you move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If he has given an answer, it's a very significant answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the beginning of March 1999, on the road between Djeneral Jankovic and Seciste, Goran Milicevic was killed from an ambush. He was a lieutenant and he was in a privately owned vehicle. Do you know anything about that killing, the beginning of March 1999?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about this. I don't know the names of the killed. Later we did hear that somebody was killed, but I don't know who it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know at least about the killing of Ziber Curri, a member of Rugova's party, the DSK, that the KLA killed also at the beginning of March 1999?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that he was killed. I don't think what you say is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that on the 27th of March, in the evening, at 1850 hours, that the terrorists attacked the police station at Stari Kacanik?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you give me the date again, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 28th of March, 1999. No, the 27th of March, 1999, at 1850 hours, the police station in Stari Kacanik was attacked.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I crossed the border on the night of the 24th of March. I don't know what happened after then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you spoke here about many things that you had heard about subsequently from your fellow citizens, from other villagers, et cetera. So it is logical that you could have heard about incidents of this nature. You have probably heard of some events. Did you hear, for example, that on the 28th of March, in Stari Kacanik, a cluster bomb was thrown and it encompassed two hectares and created about 80 craters? Are you aware of that? This is your municipality.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't heard of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you aware of anything about a terrorist attack that was carried out with hand-held rocket launchers in the street Boro Vukmirovic [phoen] in Kacanik against the police, carried out by 20 armed terrorists wearing camouflage uniforms, and nine policemen were wounded on that occasion? Are you aware of that incident?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know about an attack near the house of Enver Koka in the new neighbourhood of Kacanik? This was a terrorist attack against the members of the police when a large quantity of weapons was seized and a when a number of terrorists were liquidated? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I haven't heard of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know in your neighbourhood, in the village of Doganovici, that NATO bomb killed five persons, Albanians? Two children were seriously wounded. The children had found a cluster bomb and tried to open it and then the following persons were killed: Hoxha Fisnik, born in 1990 was killed, a child.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness deal with the question. Do you know anything about this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The village of Doganaj is not a neighbourhood of Kotlina. It's a long way away. I don't know what happened there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are we talking about the same village? I say it's the village of Doganovici. Is that the same thing?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said Doganaj is not my village. I live in Kotlina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you know anything about a cluster bomb being found by children, people being killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard that some children were wounded there, but I don't know about anybody being killed, and I know that the children were taken to Italy for treatment. But Doganaj was another village. I don't know what happened in Doganaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's now 11.00. We will adjourn. Half an hour. Would you be back, please, Mr. Loku, at half past eleven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The registrar wants to change an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The last exhibit submitted, the bundle of colour photographs, has to be numbered Exhibit 59 and the legend 59A instead of 60.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have I understood correctly that you said that you did know about the children who were the victims of the cluster bomb?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard about a cluster bomb. I know that in another village, two or three children were wounded by a bomb, but whether it was a hand grenade or what, I don't know. They went to Italy for treatment. And this -- it can be demonstrated who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do these names mean anything to you: Hoxha Fisnik, born in 1990; Hoxha Valdet, born in 1984; Hoxha Burin [phoen], 1985; Hoxha Edon, 1985; Hoxha Osman, 1985. These are the years of birth. These persons were killed and Hoxha Bersnik, 1984; and Hoxha Avdija, 1980, all from the village of Doganovici were wounded. Do these names ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know anything about them, and I don't know anything about them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I make one remark there, comment, because there seems to be misunderstanding fairly frequently with respect to names here on the transcript and geographical names, too. Let me say that geographical maps are an international resource and that you must use the names that exist on the maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know about an event that took place when the vice-president of the Municipal Board of the Socialist Party of Kacanik was kidnapped and a worker on the railway and transport company at the Kacanik station, his name was Mahmut Darlishta, with one of the Reka brothers in the Reka Brigid [phoen]. Mahmut was found dead in the village of Dure and, later on, Mahmut's son Esad was abducted. Do you know anything about those incidents?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I know nothing about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know about the kidnapping of Mile Vuksanovic from Pristina, who was otherwise a sanitary inspector who was visiting a friend of his, a hunter in the area? His name was Xhemal Strazha?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have never heard of these names or these things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard of another event when a NATO projectile hit the PTT station and destroyed the surrounding facilities in the Kacanik area? Once again, do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't heard about this, but the post office is still there and it's still working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know about the killing of Captain Milan Milenkovic in a terrorist attack by a storehouse belonging to Kacanik-Comerc, a privately owned company?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this name, and haven't heard about his murder. I know nothing about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know about six Serb families from Jankovici and 28 from Kacanik who fled to Stari Kacanik? They were fleeing the terrorists at that time. Do you know about that event?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anybody fleeing from terrorists. From Serbian terrorists, yes. Entire villages were emptied and people went to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you about the Serb families, the Serb families fleeing from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He said he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. When did you yourself return to Kacanik from Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned home from Macedonia around the middle of August, together with my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear, when you came back, that in Kacanik a retired policeman by the name of Slobodan Stojkovic had been killed, who returned from Stari Kacanik to his own apartment?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you aware of, also dating back to those days, the fact that from Stari Kacanik a group of people were kidnapped - Dragi Stankovic, with his wife Zivka and his daughter Gordana - by the village of Gajre, and that his daughter and wife were raped before his very eyes, and that they were then killed and he himself was badly wounded? Members of KFOR found the dead bodies of Zivka and Gordana by the Partizanski Put, at the junction going towards Brezovica, on the road there. Do you know about that event?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't heard about this and I don't believe such a thing happened, because the Serbian civilian population no doubt went away before the Serbian bodies arrived -- Serbian forces arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today, in Kacanik, is there a single Serb left?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were never any Serbs in Kacanik. I don't know if there are any now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were Serbs before, as you know, and I'm asking you whether there are any left now.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were Serbs in Kacanik i Vjeter, but in Kacanik itself, but apart from the policemen, there were no Serbian inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you said a moment ago that when you went to the municipality, that you would encounter only Serbs there, and they, of course, were not policemen.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They worked in the municipality. There were Serbian municipal workers, but they weren't from Kacanik. They came either from Kacanik i Vjeter or from Shterpce. They weren't from Kacanik itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But apart from those working in the municipality, you also spoke a moment ago of the fact that they were employed in companies, a company from which, as you said, the Albanians were expelled. So how come you can Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. marry the two, say that there were no Serbs and then say that there were?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will say what I said before. Except in the village of Kacanik i Vjeter, in which there were Serbs living, in the other 14 villages they were all Albanians. The population were all Albanians, and employees and policemen and the workers in the factories were Serbs. That was what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that all 40 Serb houses in Stari Kacanik were looted and burned?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw burned houses when I returned from Macedonia and passed that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you familiar with the following fact: that the KLA, after the arrival of KFOR in Kacanik, destroyed all catering establishments belonging to Albanians given to them by the Kacanik municipality, or shops?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shops were destroyed, but these were shops that were licensed by the Serbian authorities, and they were built along the river and they were built in unsuitable places. They were built along the road which connected the clinic with the town. And that was why they were pulled down. They weren't destroyed by the KLA, but they were demolished by the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know any of these names: Riza Jivoreka [phoen], Jumni Berisha [phoen], Kalishi Enver? They are all people whose shops were pulled down. Do you know any of them?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard these names, and these are people who are in Kacanik somewhere. If you need them, they can testify themselves about their shops. I know that they do have shops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that in Kacanik and Djeneral Jankovic, no facility was burned or destroyed except the house from which firing came, and there was firing at the MUP and the army, the police and the army?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can you help as to that or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand the question. But there were no houses along the main road between Kacanik and Han i Elezit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the places Kacanik and Djeneral Jankovic, those two places.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean by this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I said that not a single facility was destroyed except for one house, from which they opened fire at the members of the MUP and the army.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to know whether that is true or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He doesn't understand the question. Now, rephrase it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I claim that in Kacanik and Djeneral Jankovic, according to my information, not a single facility was destroyed, nor was it shot at, except for one house, a house from which there was shooting at members of the MUP and the army. I don't know what is not clear in that question.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I am clear about the question. You are wrong. You have got wrong information, because over half of Kacanik houses are destroyed as well as those of Han i Elezit's. They were burned by the Serb police and army forces. There are many witnesses to that. Not only the houses but people were killed and mutilated. All this was committed by your army and troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I claim the opposite. I was just asking you whether you knew about it or not. But let's move on and go on to what you said about the 24th of March. First of all, you said that the army shot from tanks, fired from tanks, but that the shells did not fall on the village itself but around the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. What is the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does he know that there were KLA positions located there?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said and I am repeating that they didn't shoot from tanks' barrels but from weapons placed on the tanks and other weapons carried by your soldiers and policemen. They shot at random. They shot at the houses of the village. They didn't shoot at a certain target because nobody was firing back at them from the village. I was there and saw everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that nobody shot -- did any shooting from the village, and my information says that seven members of the KLA, wearing uniforms, died there. Do you know about that? They were killed in the fighting that took place in the village.

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There wasn't any clashes in the village, and there weren't any KLA troops there. The KLA troops were far away in the mountains. That's why there wasn't any clash there nor any KLA members killed but only civilians were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that after that, on the spot, an investigating Judge and prosecutor from Rosevic went out to investigate and that all the documents in connection with the conflict that took place in your village and the death of those seven KLA members was sent to the Court in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He has said there were not KLA members killed. So the question involves something which he hasn't accepted. Do you know anything about the court in Pristina or anything about the investigating Judge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't seen any investigating Judges, with the exception of Serb police and army mutilating and killing innocent people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't see those seven members of the KLA that were killed there either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He said not, Mr. Milosevic. He's denied it. Now, there's no point putting it to him again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Does he know that the police, after the event, searched the pits, the holes that he's talking about, and that in those pits or holes, they just found weapons, and a large quantity at that of tins and the remnants of KLA equipment because those pits served as a basis -- as a base, sorry, base, of the KLA in Kotlina?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is all made up. The KLA never operated in our village, and whoever wished to join the KLA ranks, he might do so because the KLA troops were in the mountains. So these are all -- this is all made up by the Serb power.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those two holes or pits which they descended into with ladders, one was five metres deep, the other was seven metres deep, and they were joined together and they served as a warehouse. Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the police arrived, there were no bodies in those holes except for those weapons. How come nobody reported those dead bodies at the time?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said and can repeat many -- as many times as you wish that there were no bodies there. There were no arms there. These two holes were dug by some peasant many years ago who was looking for water, and he was unable to find any waters, but the holes remained there empty all the time. And what you are claiming here is just a concoction, I would say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You said that on that day, and I made a note of that, the soldiers left the village. How do you explain the fact then that, after the army had left the area, nobody went to those wells once the army had left? You said when the army left, you all rushed to see what was happening -- what had happened to the livestock, the cattle, but you didn't rush to see those victims that you talked about, the casualties. So how do you explain this?

utterances.speaker: HAZBI LOKU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have stated everything in my written statements. After the departure of the occupation, criminal Serb troops from the village, Chetniks and police troops, after their departure, I and others returned to the village. We knew what had happened in those holes that I talked about, but it was night. People went there to see what had happened, but it was impossible. It was very dark up in the mountain. They couldn't see anything. And it was only after some days that we realised what had happened there. We saw what had happened there. The father of Rexhep Loku, I said that his two sons were killed. He found there belong -- things belonging. I mean, it is very difficult to say what he had found. Remains of their bodies, pieces of fingers left, broken teeth, stained clothes, stained with blood, things like that, as well as a Serb cap belonging to police was found there. KFOR troops got that cap with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yesterday that when the army left, you went to see to the cattle and that nobody went towards those wells. Why did you forget the casualties of which there were some 20-odd allegedly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's just answered the question. He said some people went there but it was dark. Now, that's his answer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if you say he gave an answer, all right, but he didn't give an answer to why nobody reported it if it was true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. The question is this: It's not clear to who somebody should have reported it, but the question is why did nobody report it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't get the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I suspect it's been saying why didn't you report it to the Serb authorities? Why didn't you ring up or something of the sort?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the Serb authorities had already committed the crime. How could we report it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But the investigative Judge and the prosecutor went there to the crime scene. So wasn't it logical for someone to draw their attention to that? The investigating Judge or the prosecutor certainly had not committed any crime. They came there for an on-site investigation. How come nobody drew their attention to this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can you help us to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The village was empty. There was nobody left. People were killed. The civilian population was headed towards Kacanik. The others, like me, were hidden, were in hiding places. And I don't know if there was anyone else, with the exception of police and army troops, there. One thing we all knew, that who was captured was killed on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to your statement, there were KLA members around your village, as you had put it; there were operations between the army and the police and the KLA; and on the basis of what you've been saying, it was only civilians who were getting killed. So who was getting killed: civilians or members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think he's dealt with all this. We're now going into argument. Mr. Milosevic, you've had more than an hour and a half with this witness. Now, unless there's some new topic which is relevant, it's time to bring your cross-examination to a close.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I'll bring it to a close.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Distinguished Honour, if you want, I may give an answer to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. You've dealt with all these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
